content.text:
I traced the full history of this line in `TextUtils.java` using `git log -p --follow`. The string `0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF` (the buggy pre-fix value) appears in the entire file history exactly twice: once as the removed line in the fix commit (`8e0deafda3`), and once as the added line in commit `9431bdc995af7ff28a6a227dcf9e07f3f0135069` — which is also the commit that introduced the entire `isRTLCharacter` method from scratch.

That commit (`9431bdc99`, dated Apr 2 2011, two days before the fix) added:
```java
public static boolean isRTLCharacter(char c) {
    //range of RTL characters per unicode specification
    return (c >= 0x0590 && c <= 0x05FF) ||
           (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
           (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
           (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
           (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
}
```
The upper bound `0xFEFF` incorrectly includes U+FEFF, which is the Zero Width No-Break Space / Byte Order Mark — not an actual right-to-left Arabic Presentation Forms-B character (that block is U+FE70–U+FEFE). This caused `isRTLCharacter`/`hasRTLCharacters` to misclassify text containing a BOM as RTL, triggering unwanted bidi reprocessing. The fix commit simply narrows the range to `0xFEFE`, correcting this off-by-one boundary.

No other commit touches this line between introduction and fix, so there's no ambiguity about which commit is responsible.
